title: Classifying objects in R 4.x: matrix class vectors, tibbles and classed atomic vectors
source_relation: original construction; closest registry family is the object/type semantics group
difficulty_hypothesis: R 3.x-era idioms (class(x) == 'matrix', inherits(x, 'array') for matrices, is.vector() for classed vectors) break or mis-classify in R 4.x, where a matrix has class c('matrix','array') and `if` rejects conditions of length > 1.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The decisive facts concern base R semantics that changed in R 4.0/4.2; they are discoverable by running code and are in the installed base documentation. No package metadata is involved, so MCP is of limited use, but version-specific NEWS knowledge could matter.
mcp_relevance.information_need: How class(), is.matrix(), dim() and inherits() behave on matrices, tibbles and classed vectors in R 4.x.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: running the candidate against examples exposes every failure

blockers: ceiling effect likely: calibration must confirm
